newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: WORLD BANK LAUDS GOV'T REFORM PROGRAMME.
newsitem.headline: WORLD BANK LAUDS GOV'T REFORM PROGRAMME.

text.p: The Lithuanian government said on Wednesday that the World Bank applauded its steps to speed up reforms and complete the country's transition to a market economy.

"Clear, positive changes are seen in the work of the present government," the government's press office quoted Basil Kovalsky, a director with the World Bank's Europe and Asia department, as saying in a statement.
Kovalsky is part of a World Bank mission currently visiting Lithuania to examine its economic reform programme.
The statement said that the World Bank welcomed the government's efforts to reform Lithuania's energy and banking sectors and push the privatisation of large enterprises.
It added that the World Bank recommended that the government focus more attention on reforming the country's pension system and lay the groundwork for the creation of private pension plans.
Like many former Communist states, Lithuania's state pension system is burdened by a growing number of pensioners and a lack of funds, a situation which has thrown many elderly people into poverty.
